title: Novel Therapeutic Strategies for Traumatic Brain Injury: From Conventional Treatment to Astrocyte Reprogramming
content: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a global health problem characterized by high disability and mortality. The action of the main damaging factor, the shock wave, causes several primary changes: changes in cerebrospinal fluid production and cerebral hemodynamic disorders, increased vascular permeability, and disruption of subcortical structure functions. This results in brain edema. Secondary brain injury is a response to the primary injury. Neuroinflammation is an important pathological component of secondary brain injury. These events result in delayed damage and death of neural cells. In this review, we examined TBI pathogenesis and the conservative approaches used to treat it. Separate chapters of the review are devoted to the analysis of experimental data on neurogenesis and the neurogenic potential of astrocytes. Astrocytes are considered by some researchers to be a potential source of new neurons. This makes them a promising target for developing new approaches aimed at restoring lost neurons after TBI. Among existing approaches, of particular interest is the use of small molecules to reprogram astrocytes into neurons. The review discusses different small-molecule cocktail compositions and their effects, as well as the main limitations hindering the development and translation of reprogramming technology. Furthermore, the review proposes that a sequential use of anti-inflammatory therapy and small molecules delivered via synthetic carriers may be rational for neuroregeneration post-TBI.
